newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH GDANSK REFINERY WORKERS READY FOR STRIKE.
newsitem.headline: POLISH GDANSK REFINERY WORKERS READY FOR STRIKE.

text.p: A referendum among workers of Poland's second largest Gdansk refinery showed 88 percent of those polled were ready to go on strike to get the firm's shares and a pay rise in 1997, a union official said.

Andrzej Cenacewicz, head of the Solidarity trade union in the Gdansk Refinery, told Reuters that four trade unions active in the company polled 1159 employees, or 79.3 percent of all workers, over a week.
"The workers of the Gdansk refinery are ready to go on strike," Cenacewicz said.

The unions demand 15 percent of the refinery's shares for free which, they say, should be given to them in line with the new privatisation law after the refinery's shares had been alloted to the state-owned Nafta Polska oil holding last year.
The new privatisation law, however, does not come into force until April 8.

"The refinery's workers may be worrying unnecessarily. Once the new law is in place, it is very likely that the relevant ministry will launch procedures to give the shares to workers," an senior Nafta official, who asked not to be named, said.
Nafta has 75 percent of the refinery's shares and is itself owned by the finance ministry.

It was not immediately clear, however, if the remaining 25 percent of Gdansk shares, out of which the employee stock would be paid out, were at the disposal of the finance or the treasury ministry after the recent administration reform.

The refinery's workers also want the management to raise their wages by 17 percent this year as envisaged by the agreement struck by employers, unions and the government in the three-sided committee last year.
Gdansk refinery's spokeswoman Ewa Sielicka said the company's board had no comment on the results of the referendum.
"But the board is waiting for proposals (from trade unions) on the line-up of its negotiating team," Sielicka said.
She declined to comment on what effects a potential strike could have on Gdansk's production.
